frontmatter_description: Direct-route macro for judging trust, reputation, identity, role, and relationship decisions from long-term interaction history.
title: Trust, Relationship, and Long-Term Interaction
use_when: Use when the question depends on a person's reputation, reliability, loyalty, role, or history with others.
Use when past interactions change how the character should be judged now.
Use when long-term relationship context matters more than a single statement, single event, or one-time credibility cue.
Use when the scene asks who to trust, how to interpret behavior in a relationship, or how history should affect future interaction.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when the core issue is a live misunderstanding that should be clarified immediately in conversation.
Do not use when the main issue is apology, compensation, or repairing damage after an offense.
Do not use when the case is mainly about spatial perspective, quantity estimation, or a one-off belief update without relationship history.
Do not use when the task is only to judge whether one statement is true from a single source of evidence.
decision_variable: how long-term history affects trust, reputation, identity, role, and relationship judgment
direct_route_rule: Route immediately when trust, reputation, identity, role, or long-term relational history matters.
trigger_checklist: The scene mentions past behavior, repeated interaction, or a known track record.
The answer depends on whether someone is trustworthy, loyal, reliable, or credible over time.
A relationship label, social role, or reputation changes the interpretation of the current event.
The question is about how to treat someone now based on history, not just the current utterance.
There is a distinction between temporary behavior and stable relational pattern.
workflow: Identify the long-term relationship variable: trust, loyalty, reputation, identity, or role.
Collect the history signal: repeated actions, prior promises, known patterns, and social standing.
Weigh history over isolated surface cues unless the scene explicitly overrides history.
Infer the most reasonable relationship judgment or action based on accumulated evidence.
If the case is actually about a narrower sub-skill such as credibility, apology, or live clarification, exit to the relevant micro or neighboring macro.

special_case.title: Mixed history with one new event
special_case.rule: When a single new event conflicts with a long record, the long-term pattern usually sets the baseline unless the scene states a decisive rupture, verified betrayal, or formal role change.

worked_example.scene: A coworker has been dependable for years but misses one deadline after a family emergency.
worked_example.question: Should their reliability be judged as bad now?
worked_example.answer_logic: Use the long-term record as the main signal. The one missed deadline is a temporary exception, not enough by itself to replace the established trust pattern.

boundary_exit_rule: Exit to macro-08 / micro-37 if the task is really about whether one statement is true or false from a single source.
Exit to macro-17 if the scene is a repair conversation, apology, or reconciliation after harm.
Exit to macro-16 if the main issue is clarifying a misunderstanding in real time.
Exit to macro-19 if the question is about first impression only and no relationship history is available.
Exit to macro-01 / macro-07 / macro-20 if another macro better captures the core (false belief, indirect meaning, or power-distance communication).
Add micro-18 when single-source credibility within a longer relationship is the deciding factor.
Add micro-44 when fairness or reciprocity history controls the judgment.
Add micro-45 when long-term reliability or reputation must be diagnosed.
Add micro-46 when the role or status structure of the relationship matters.
Add micro-47 when group identity changes how history is read.
Add micro-56 when causal attribution across the history is required.

references.route_signal: Long-term history, reputation, loyalty, trustworthiness, role, or identity determines the answer.
hard_boundary: Single-source credibility is not enough by itself.
A one-off lie or one-off mistake does not automatically make this a relationship-history case.
If the scene is mainly about apology or damage repair, it belongs outside this macro.
If the scene is mainly about live clarification of misunderstanding, it belongs outside this macro.
shortcut_to_avoid: Do not answer from the most recent event alone.
Do not treat trust as a pure truth-checking problem.
Do not ignore the established relationship baseline.
Do not collapse role, reputation, and trust into generic belief reasoning.
common_failure_modes: Overweighting a single new action and forgetting the track record.
Confusing reputation judgment with literal truth assessment.
Routing apology or reconciliation scenes here when repair is the real target.
Treating role-based trust as mere familiarity rather than a long-term pattern.

minimal_pair.case: A manager must decide whether to assign a sensitive task to an employee who has been reliable for years.
minimal_pair.why_it_matches: The answer depends on long-term trust and reputation, not a one-off statement.

minimal_pair.case: A manager just met a new contractor and must decide whether to assign a sensitive task based only on a single recommendation letter.
minimal_pair.why_it_matches: This is a near miss: there is no track record, only single-source credibility, so it routes to macro-19 or micro-18 rather than to long-term relationship judgment.

boundary_stress_test: If the scene gives only one statement from a stranger, this macro should usually not be used.
If the scene is about whether to apologize, compensate, or reconcile after offense, leave this macro.
If the scene asks what someone means by a remark, do not solve it here unless trust history is the main reason.
references.generalization_note: This macro generalizes to any scene where accumulated interaction history changes trust, reputation, role expectations, or relationship judgment, even when the wording differs from benchmark-style prompts.

validation_seed.positive_pattern: A character must decide how much to trust or rely on someone based on a repeated history of behavior, reputation, loyalty, or role.
validation_seed.near_miss_pattern: A character must interpret one ambiguous statement or one isolated action without any meaningful relationship history.
validation_seed.boundary_pattern: A relationship has been harmed and the scene is mainly about apology, repair, or reconciliation rather than judgment from long-term history.

notes: This is a direct scene prototype, not a micro bundle.
Use micro expansions only for diagnosis or boundary repair when the scene turns on a narrower subcase.
The core answer logic is historical: stable pattern first, isolated event second.
Preserve the distinction between trust over time and single-event credibility.
core_question: how long-term history affects trust, reputation, and relationship judgment
